title: Teach Study Prove
opening: A clear explanation can teach a relationship. A different situation can test where it applies. An actual attempt can show what happened there. Keep those jobs distinct when you reuse an idea.

labels.mapIntro: Choose a job to inspect. They answer different questions; an explanation or one successful attempt does not establish generality.
labels.sourceQuote: You can make learning useful in three ways: teach the relationship clearly, study how it works in another situation, and prove an application through an actual pursuit.
labels.reuse: Carry it into a changed situation
labels.reuseIntro: Record the changed conditions and actual evidence before reusing the relationship. Keep the limits visible; one application does not prove every case.
labels.practice: Apply this to a real idea
labels.practiceIntro: Describe what you taught, the different situation you studied, an actual pursuit where you applied it, and what should change in the shared explanation.

steps.title: Teach the relationship clearly
steps.detail: State the relationship, its reasoning, and an example that makes the claim inspectable. Label an explanation as teaching, not proof of effect.

steps.title: Study another situation
steps.detail: Choose a relevant case with changed conditions. Examine what remains useful and what differs; do not rename the principle to make it fit.

steps.title: Apply it in an actual pursuit
steps.detail: Carry the relationship into real work and inspect what happens under the recorded conditions. A fictional story or worked example is not observed application.

steps.title: Return the correction and limits
steps.detail: Use new evidence to improve, narrow, or overturn the shared explanation. Keep attribution and uncertainty; one success does not establish universality.

fields.label: What relationship, reasoning, and example did you teach?
What different situation did you study, and what conditions changed?
What actual pursuit used the relationship, and what happened?
What correction, limit, or uncertainty should return to the shared explanation?
What new-condition evidence would justify reusing it elsewhere?

example.teach: Explain how deliberate preparation can free attention during a performance, and why.
example.study: Examine a different skill where preparation and performance interact; note that the task and feedback conditions differ.
example.prove: In an actual practice, observe whether a learner can use the distinction under the stated conditions. Do not claim this observation caused a later result.
example.limits: If the distinction fails when conditions change, narrow the claim and retain what is unknown.
example.return: Use the relationship in another real pursuit only after recording its changed conditions and observing what the recipient can do there.

source.assessmentBoundary: Six required open-ended course questions remain separate from this optional private note. No qualified semantic grade or learner outcome is supplied.
